turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so I'll be brief: why is there a zero on Owen's essay, and why did I learn about it from my son's phone?
I didn't come to be thanked. Answer the question, Hale: who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Owen is a great kid. Really bright, one of my favourites.
"Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?"
I'm sure this is all just a misunderstanding.
A misunderstanding. A zero in the gradebook is a decision, Hale, and I'm writing that down. What is it based on?
So can we agree he's a good student?
You're leading me, Hale. I've done this for twenty years. I asked what the zero is based on, and I'm still waiting.
